title: Alpha Box Office: Alia Bhatt's Spy Thriller Crashes With 81% Second-Week Drop, Earns ₹57 Crore in 14 Days
excerpt: YRF's first female-led spy film collected just ₹8.95 crore in its second week, putting it on track for a lifetime total well below its ₹100 crore production budget.
body:
Key Takeaways
  • Alpha earned ₹8.95 crore in its second week, an 81.5% drop from its opening week.
  • Total 14-day domestic collection stands at ₹57.35 crore net, with ₹95 crore worldwide.
  • The film's estimated ₹100 crore budget indicates significant financial losses ahead.
  • Alpha's second-week decline is less severe than War 2's 85.9% drop.
  • Audience fatigue with the Spy Universe brand contributed to Alpha's poor performance.

  • Total 14-day domestic collection stands at ₹57.35 crore net (₹67.67 crore gross), with ₹27.37 crore from overseas for a worldwide total of ₹95 crore.
  • Made on an estimated ₹100 crore budget, the film is headed for significant losses for Yash Raj Films.
  • Alpha performed marginally better than War 2, which saw an 85.9% second-week drop, but the YRF Spy Universe is in clear commercial distress.

Alia Bhatt and Sharvari's Alpha has wrapped its second week at the Indian box office with numbers that confirm what the opening week hinted at: YRF's first female-led spy film is a commercial disappointment that will end its theatrical run deep in the red.

The Numbers

Alpha earned an estimated ₹60 lakh on Day 14 (second Thursday), bringing its second-week total to ₹8.95 crore — an 81.5% plunge from the ₹48.4 crore opening week. The domestic net total after 14 days stands at ₹57.35 crore, converting to ₹67.67 crore gross.

Overseas collections have been marginally better, adding ₹27.37 crore gross to push the worldwide total to roughly ₹95 crore. But against an estimated production budget of ₹100 crore — before prints, advertising, and marketing costs — the film is tracking toward substantial losses for producer Aditya Chopra and Yash Raj Films.

How It Compares

Within the YRF Spy Universe, Alpha's second-week decline of 81.5% is actually less severe than War 2, which crashed 85.9% in its second week after earning ₹209 crore in an extended opening week. But the comparison offers cold comfort: War 2 had a much larger first-week base, while Alpha's opening was already modest for a big-budget franchise entry.

Trade analysts project Alpha's lifetime domestic collection will settle between ₹55 crore and ₹60 crore net — less than what Tiger 3 collected in its opening weekend alone.

What Went Wrong

Several factors converged against Alpha. The YRF Spy Universe brand arrived at a low ebb after Tiger 3 and War 2 both underperformed relative to their predecessors. Audience fatigue with the franchise's formulaic approach — globe-trotting action sequences, surprise cameos, interconnected timeline reveals — has been building since Pathaan's success in 2023 proved to be more of a Shah Rukh Khan comeback than a Spy Universe rally.

Alpha attempted to differentiate itself with a female-led cast. Alia Bhatt plays Sita, a trained soldier uncovering dark truths about her past, while Sharvari plays her estranged sister Durga. Bobby Deol and Anil Kapoor round out the supporting cast, with Hrithik Roshan making a cameo. Director Shiv Rawail, working with his first feature of this scale, faced an uphill battle against audience skepticism.

Industry observers noted that historically, female-led action films have struggled at the Indian box office, making the project inherently risky regardless of star power.

The Spy Universe's Future

The back-to-back struggles of War 2 and Alpha raise fundamental questions about the franchise's commercial viability. What began as a shared cinematic universe — India's answer to Marvel — has now produced two consecutive underperformers after Pathaan.

For the diaspora audience, the box office trajectory matters beyond entertainment. Weak domestic performance typically results in shortened international theatrical runs, fewer screens, and delayed OTT releases. Alpha's overseas gross of ₹27.37 crore, while respectable, falls well short of the figures that would justify expanded global distribution for future installments.

Alpha's third week is expected to see further steep declines, with most screens likely to be reclaimed by new releases.
